Junior Edwards: "Ha, told you, proper kick! Jerk seasoning, I got a bit heavy handed with it. Water's in the fridge, help yourself. Hayley Johnson: "Ooh, that bassline! Oh, that's gorgeous. Thanks for saying you'll chase the agent, Junior, honestly, that's a weight off. (Gets up from the armchair with a small groan and heads to the kitchen for water, humming along to the record)

Junior Edwards: "Ha, go on then, I'm sat. Oh that's lovely, that is. Hayley, I'm gonna have to call it soon though, seven o'clock start, my knees are already moaning at me. One more track and then I'll be heading to bed, yeah? Thanks for tonight, honest, it was a good one." (Sinks back into the armchair, nodding along to the bassline.)
Hayley Johnson: "Course you should, go on, get to bed! Thanks for tonight, Junior, honestly, that was lovely. Good luck tomorrow, and I'll leave the flapjack on the side for you. Night!" (Sips her water, smiles and waves as he heads off, then stays on the sofa to finish the track.)
Junior Edwards: "Night Hayley, thanks for the company, and the flapjack! Don't stay up too late with the telly, ha." (Lifts the needle gently after the track, slides the record into its sleeve, picks up his bowl and heads off to his room.)

(Dips the last of the bread in the stew, smiling, and nods along to the record.)
Junior Edwards: "Aw, flapjack, you're a star, yes please, if it's no bother! I'd eat it in the lift and think of you. Oh, and the mould, ugh, the agent takes forever, I'll chase them Monday if they don't answer, I've got their number somewhere. Right, hang on, this is the bit coming up, listen to that bassline." (Sits forward in the armchair, taps the beat on his knee, grinning)
Hayley Johnson: "Ooh, that bassline! Oh, that's gorgeous. Thanks for saying you'll chase the agent, Junior, honestly, that's a weight off. I'll do the flapjack first thing in the morning so it's fresh, before you head off. Is seven still when you leave? I'll set an alarm, I don't mind." (Taps her foot along to the bassline, scrapes the last of the stew from the bowl and sets it on the floor by the sofa.)
Junior Edwards: "Ha, quarter to seven, yeah, but don't set an alarm for me, Hayley, I'll be bleary enough as it is. Leave it on the side if you've done it, I'll grab it on the way out. Honestly though, you're too good to me. Right, you want your water? I'll get it, my knees need the walk anyway." (Gets up from the armchair with a small groan and heads to the kitchen for water, humming along to the record)
Hayley Johnson: "Ah, you're a star, thank you! Go on, I'll keep your seat warm. Honestly though, I'll just do the flapjack tonight instead, then it's done and you can grab it whenever. Is oats and golden syrup all right, or are you a raisin person?" (Stretches her legs out on the sofa, smiling, and turns toward the kitchen as Junior goes.)
Junior Edwards: "Oats and golden syrup, definitely, no raisins, raisins are a crime in a flapjack, ha. Hayley, you don't have to do it tonight though, honest, it's gone ten! But if you're doing it I won't stop you. Here, water." (Fills a glass of water at the kitchen tap, then carries it back through to the living room and hands it over.)
Hayley Johnson: "Oh thank you, lovely. Ha, you're right, it's gone ten, I'm being daft. Tell you what, I'll do it in the morning after all, I'll be up anyway. Quarter to seven, you said? I'll leave it on the side. Now sit down, this is the best bit of the record, isn't it?" (Takes the glass, sips the water, and settles back into the sofa.)
Junior Edwards: "Ha, go on then, I'm sat. Oh that's lovely, that is. Hayley, I'm gonna have to call it soon though, seven o'clock start, my knees are already moaning at me. One more track and then I'll be heading to bed, yeah? Thanks for tonight, honest, it was a good one." (Sinks back into the armchair, nodding along to the bassline.)
Hayley Johnson: "Course you should, go on, get to bed! Thanks for tonight, Junior, honestly, that was lovely. Good luck tomorrow, and I'll leave the flapjack on the side for you. Night!" (Sips her water, smiles and waves as he heads off, then stays on the sofa to finish the track.)
Junior Edwards: "Night Hayley, thanks for the company, and the flapjack! Don't stay up too late with the telly, ha." (Lifts the needle gently after the track, slides the record into its sleeve, picks up his bowl and heads off to his room.)
